PullRequest.Title: Agent Host: stop delivering standalone customizations as plugin content
PullRequest.Body:
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8826

**TL;DR:** VS Code bundles the skills, agents, and MCP servers it forwards into a synthetic "VS Code Synced Data" plugin (`SyncedCustomizationBundler`), and the Agent Host passes it in `pluginDirectories`. The runtime loads those skills as plugin skills, so the `skills` lockdown skipped them. Forwarded MCP servers were already registered through session config, and bundled agents weren't exposed. Fix: send user/workspace skills and agents, and all forwarded MCP servers, through `skillDirectories`, `customAgents`, and `mcpServers`, so the runtime filters them itself. Extension and built-in skills and agents stay in the synced plugin.

### Current flow

- `resolveCustomizationRefs` bundles loose skills, agents, instructions, prompt files, and forwarded MCP servers into "VS Code Synced Data".
- The Copilot Agent Host copies the bundle to disk and passes it in `pluginDirectories`.
- The runtime loads those skills as plugin skills, so the `skills` lock doesn't apply. MCP servers already go through session config, and agents in the bundle aren't exposed.

### New flow

- User/workspace skills and agents, plus every forwarded MCP server, go to a second bundle marked with `_meta` `vscode.standaloneCustomizations: true`.
- For that bundle, the host drops `pluginDir`, so skills go through `skillDirectories`, agents through `customAgents`, and MCP servers through session `mcpServers`, where the runtime applies the lockdown. `resourceDir` keeps reads of its files auto-approved.
- Extension and built-in skills and agents, instructions, and prompt files stay in "VS Code Synced Data".
- Hosts that ignore the marker (Claude, Codex) keep treating the bundle as a plugin.

### Not in this PR

- Array support in the workbench (Local harness and UI), which still reads only the boolean setting.
- Hooks: VS Code doesn't forward them, so the runtime already governs the ones it discovers.

### Risks

- Behavior change: forwarded agents now reach the runtime, so without a lockdown they're available as subagents.
- The `customAgents` converter carries name, description, model, reasoning effort, tools, skills, `infer`, and the prompt; other agent frontmatter is dropped.
- Ephemeral sessions (inline and terminal chat) skip `customAgents` and session-config MCP servers, so moved agents and MCP servers don't reach them.
- Moved items get a new client plugin URI, so host-side enablement may reset once.

### How to test

Manual before/after verification with screenshots: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/340079#issuecomment-6021290444

1. Serve `{"strictPluginOnlyCustomization": ["skills", "agents", "mcp"]}` through the mock policy server (`.github/skills/policy-and-managed-settings/local-testing.md`).
2. Configure a skill and an agent with `chat.agentSkillsLocations` and `chat.agentFilesLocations`, add a server to the user `mcp.json`, and start a Copilot Agent Host session.
3. `/env` shouldn't list the skill or the server, and the model can't run the agent. Without the lockdown, all three work.

Automated: the targeted suites pass (93, 1524, and 1878 passing), and ESLint is clean. `npm run typecheck-client` reports no new errors; my local `node_modules` is stale, so CI is the real check.

Inspirations from:

- The `_meta` marker and its reader follow the [`mcpDefaultCwds` client plugin meta](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c1239d20320a6bdfd739cfa4ac8d5b4040772ce2/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/meta/vscode/clientPluginCustomizationMeta.ts#L9-L56).
- Standalone delivery reuses the launcher's [`pluginsWithoutDirs` path](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c1239d20320a6bdfd739cfa4ac8d5b4040772ce2/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSessionLauncher.ts#L995-L1013) into `skillDirectories` and `customAgents`.
- MCP servers already registered through session config: [`resolveCopilotMcpServerInfo`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c1239d20320a6bdfd739cfa4ac8d5b4040772ce2/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts#L240-L249).
- What counts as standalone matches the workbench lockdown in [`areStandalonePromptFilesBlocked`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c1239d20320a6bdfd739cfa4ac8d5b4040772ce2/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/promptSyntax/service/promptsServiceImpl.ts#L526-L545) and [`McpRegistry.isCollectionAllowed`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c1239d20320a6bdfd739cfa4ac8d5b4040772ce2/src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/common/mcpRegistry.ts#L498-L501).
- `resourceDir` keeps the read trust from [`_isReadWithinAppliedPluginDirectory`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c1239d20320a6bdfd739cfa4ac8d5b4040772ce2/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L5375-L5389).

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed conditional, the sole recursive-delete site, the no-op disposal behavior, and the process-wide provider ownership are all directly traced. The exact prevalence and bundle sizes vary, which limits severity, but retention on the stated transition is deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: In-memory filesystem nodes and VSBuffer contents for removed skill/agent resources
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retained memory grows with the recursive size of the last standalone bundle (skill directories include all files except .git and node_modules) and with the number/lifetime of affected workspace scopes; the process-wide filesystem provider keeps those trees reachable until window shutdown.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: retained memory and avoidable memory pressure after customizations are removed
Findings.PreviousBehavior: With one combined bundler, if a user removed the last standalone skill/agent while any instruction, prompt, extension skill, or other loose file remained, resolveCustomizationRefs still called bundle(looseFiles, mcpServers); _bundle deleted and rewrote the authority root, releasing the removed files.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The split only invokes the standalone bundler while standaloneFiles or mcpServers is non-empty. When that partition transitions to empty but the synced partition remains, no operation reaches the standalone bundler, so its previous root and reverse-origin map remain populated.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added standalone conditional at RIGHT line 339 partitions the former single `if (looseFiles.length > 0 || mcpServers.length > 0) bundler.bundle(...)` call. For a state change from {standalone skill + synced instruction} to {synced instruction}, the old call rebuilt the shared root without the skill, while the new code calls only `bundlers.synced.bundle` and never clears the standalone authority.
Findings.Title: Clear a partition when its last customization is removed
Findings.Impact: Removing a configured user/workspace skill can leave the skill's recursively copied assets resident for the rest of the VS Code window. Large skills or many long-lived workspace scopes retain correspondingly more memory even though the customization is no longer advertised.
Findings.Evidence: Line 339 skips bundlers.standalone.bundle entirely for an empty partition. SyncedCustomizationBundler._bundle is the only path that calls fileService.del(this._rootUri, { recursive: true }) and clears _originByDest; its early empty check also has no reset behavior. SyncedCustomizationBundler.dispose only disposes its limiter, and AgentHostFileSystemService owns one process-wide InMemoryFileSystemProvider, so an omitted empty transition leaves the prior tree strongly reachable.
Findings.Recommendation: Give each bundler an explicit empty/reset operation that deletes its authority root and clears `_lastNonce`, `_lastRef`, and `_originByDest`, and invoke it whenever that partition becomes empty (or make `bundle([], [])` perform this cleanup).

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial customization resolution and live updates after adding, editing, or removing skills, agents, instructions, prompts, or forwarded MCP servers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial resolution must finish before the active client publishes its customization refs; live updates are debounced 50 ms and publish only after enumeration, MCP collection, bundle hashing, and any required in-memory rewrites complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate skill directories, stat and read source files, hash contents, and write copies into the process-wide in-memory synced-customization filesystem
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolve/stat per traversed skill directory and roughly one stat/read per included asset; writes occur once per file only on a nonce change, now split across up to two bundle roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same source contents were read and hashed through one bundler with one 10-operation limiter and one root; one combined non-empty call also removed files that disappeared from either category.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All reads and hashes block initial or updated customization publication; rewrites block only on cold/change misses.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retain copied files and reverse-origin metadata in the singleton InMemoryFileSystemProvider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one tree per partition per workspace/session-type scope; retained bytes scale with recursive skill assets in the last populated partition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: When another loose category remained, the single combined bundle was rebuilt and its recursive root deletion released files removed from the now-empty category.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the immediate critical path after publication, but retained for the window lifetime and contributes memory pressure.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled loose customization files plus every recursively discovered skill asset, partitioned into synced and standalone sets; effective cardinality is the total source-file count after plugin-owned entries are deduplicated into plugin refs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two partition bundles are awaited together. Each authority is independently sequenced and each bundler has its own 10-operation filesystem limiter, so mixed content can issue up to 20 source filesystem operations concurrently; updates for the same authority serialize.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each partition rereads and hashes its files on every resolution. A matching per-partition nonce skips delete/write work, but an empty partition is not invoked or invalidated, leaving its previous tree and metadata reachable; this is the reported regression.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: conditional invocation, the sole recursive-delete path, no cleanup in bundler disposal, and singleton provider ownership were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical skill asset sizes and the number of simultaneous workspace scopes vary; the empty-partition retention mechanism itself is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable memory-retention regression when either new partition transitions to empty while the other remains.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot Agent Host synchronization and session launch with both synced-plugin and standalone customizations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The host waits for client customization synchronization/parsing and applied-plugin resolution before building session configuration; custom-agent file conversion is also awaited before createSession/resumeSession.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy each synthetic customization tree from the client-backed agent filesystem URI to host-local plugin cache storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold path increases from one synthetic tree copy to as many as two parallel tree copies; aggregate content is partitioned rather than duplicated, plus one extra manifest/root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A single synthetic bundle ref carried all loose files and forwarded MCP configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold copies and parsing block customization settlement/session launch; nonce hits avoid tree copies but still touch and persist the LRU.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse each standalone custom-agent markdown file into SDK customAgents
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential read per standalone agent on non-ephemeral session launch; selected file-dir agents were already read individually when needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These agents stayed under pluginDirectories and were generally discovered by the SDK rather than projected by the host; total runtime discovery work still scaled with the same agents, so no high-confidence net performance regression was established.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited while building session config, in parallel with independent BYOK and shell-tool setup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Up to two synthetic bundle refs instead of one, with total content partitioned; launch conversion scales with parsed standalone agents, skills, and MCP definitions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: AgentPluginManager copies refs in parallel and serializes only by URI. Session custom agents are read sequentially inside toSdkCustomAgents, while that conversion runs in parallel with BYOK and shell-tool setup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Content nonces let AgentPluginManager skip copies for warm revisions; its disk LRU is shared and bounded. Standalone agent conversion has no separate content cache per session. Bundler nonces are stable per partition.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the changed call paths and cardinality; insufficient evidence that the partitioning overhead produces material latency beyond the separate retention finding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The latency difference between one and two copy roots and between SDK discovery and explicit agent projection depends on host locality and runtime implementation; total payload bytes are nearly unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the extra root/setup overhead is bounded, warm copies are cached, and total customization content is not duplicated.

Scenarios.Scenario: Runtime loading and policy filtering of standalone skills, agents, and forwarded MCP servers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Skill paths, custom-agent configs, and MCP server configs are supplied in the SDK session configuration. Enabled MCP server startup/discovery can affect runtime readiness; policy-blocked standalone items are filtered by the runtime.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch enabled local forwarded MCP server commands from session mcpServers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one runtime registration/start per enabled forwarded server; the logical server set is unchanged by the diff, and lockdown can reduce it to zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Forwarded MCP definitions were already resolved and registered through session configuration even while the same synthetic root was also passed as a plugin directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Server initialization may affect runtime tool availability/readiness, but the diff changes provenance/delivery rather than server count.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve real paths to auto-approve reads contained within applied plugin or standalone resource directories
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One containment check per applied plugin/resource directory for a read permission request; resourceDir replaces pluginDir for the standalone bundle, so directory count is unchanged for that bundle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same standalone bundle directory participated through pluginDir; it now participates through resourceDir.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on read-permission handling, not session startup; first matching directory can complete the parallel check.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of standalone skills, agents, and enabled forwarded MCP servers after host/workbench enablement and name deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: MCP process startup concurrency is runtime-owned; this diff does not add a host limiter or increase the number of logical forwarded servers. Plugin synchronization remains parallel per distinct bundle URI.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Workbench and host bundle nonces cache unchanged content. MCP process lifecycle and runtime discovery caching are outside the reviewed diff; negative/blocked policy results do not create host-side retry loops here.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that server cardinality and permission-check directory cardinality do not increase due to this delivery change.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime MCP startup scheduling and SDK internal discovery costs are not visible in this repository.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff changes classification and policy enforcement without increasing logical MCP launches or containment checks.

Scenarios.Scenario: Claude/Codex or other hosts that ignore the standalone metadata marker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: These hosts receive and synchronize both synthetic refs, then continue treating each as a plugin before their session becomes ready.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize two client plugin roots rather than one when both partitions are populated
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two roots versus one, with partitioned aggregate file bytes and one additional manifest.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All loose content was represented by one synthetic plugin root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds bounded per-root setup on a cold sync, while independent nonce reuse can avoid retransmitting the unchanged partition on later updates.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Same total loose customization files and MCP definitions split over up to two roots.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Host plugin synchronization can process the two independent refs concurrently; exact downstream plugin loading concurrency is host-specific.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each root has an independent content nonce, allowing unchanged partitions to remain warm instead of invalidating one combined nonce.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the one-to-two root change; low that it causes a material net slowdown.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host-specific setup overhead is unknown, and partition-level cache reuse can offset the extra root.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: bounded extra root metadata is balanced by finer-grained nonce reuse, with no duplicated payload established.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 13 changed files. One deterministic cleanup-lifecycle regression was submitted: an emptied new partition is not reset, retaining removed customization assets in the process-wide in-memory filesystem. Other changed startup, IPC/filesystem, SDK conversion, MCP subprocess, cache, and concurrency paths did not establish an additional material regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
